steps.title: Yes, it is farther
steps.say: Good catch — in northern summer, Earth is actually a bit farther from the Sun than in January.

ops.text:
Yes! In July Earth is ~5 million km farther
from the Sun than in January.

steps.title: Distance isn't the driver
steps.say: So distance can't be the main cause. What really matters is the angle of the sunlight.

ops.text:
What matters: the ANGLE of sunlight,
not the distance.

steps.title: Tilt toward the Sun
steps.say: In northern summer, the north pole leans toward the Sun, so sunlight hits the north at a steep, direct angle.

ops.text: Northern summer: north pole leans toward Sun

steps.title: Tilt away: winter
steps.say: Six months later the north pole leans away, so sunlight comes in at a shallow angle and spreads out.

ops.text: Northern winter: north pole leans away
Sunlight hits at a shallow angle — spread out

steps.title: The takeaway
steps.say: Steeper sunlight packs more energy into each patch of ground, and the days are longer too. That's why summer is hot.

ops.text: Steep sunlight = more energy per patch + longer days = hotter summer.
